extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in number theory/arithmetic geometry (readers of Mochizuki's IUT papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Formal properties, compatibility conditions, and constructional requirements for log-links, log-shells, and associated (D-/F-) prime-strips in Mochizuki's IUT framework. Includes local (archimedean/nonarchimedean) and global statements, algorithmic constructions, and structural incompatibilities (the log-wall).

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautological log-link
rubrics_metrics.description: The diagram †Fv  log−→  log(†Fv) — the relationship between †Fv and log(†Fv) obtained by the tautological construction; referred to as the tautological log-link associated to †Fv (or, when †F is fixed, at v).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tautological log-link gives a tautological identification between the †Πv’s appearing in the data of the domain and codomain of the tautological log-link (see Remark 1.2.1 (i)). It is the basic/tautological correspondence used to relate †Fv and its log-object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full log-link (post-composed log-link)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given a [poly-]isomorphism log(†Fv) ∼→ ‡Fv, the diagram obtained by post-composing the tautological log-link with this [poly-]isomorphism is denoted †Fv  log−→  ‡Fv and called a log-link from †Fv to ‡Fv; if the [poly-]isomorphism is the full poly-isomorphism, the result is the full log-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper works mainly with the full log-link (not the tautological one) because, in multiradial algorithms (§3), it is crucial to express relationships between the ´etale-like (−)Πv’s in purely ´etale-like terms free of dependence on Frobenius-like monoids — this is achieved by the tautologically indeterminate isomorphism underlying the full log-link.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-shell associated to †Fv
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-shell is the compact topological subquotient (determined by the submonoid of units Ψ×) of Ψ∼ (or equivalently the Ψ×-log(†Fv)-orbit of a uniquely determined closed line segment whose endpoints differ by a generator of ker(Ψ∼ → Ψgp) or its N-multiple).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One may think of the log-shell as an object associated to the codomain of any log-link — it is determined by the image of a certain portion (the subquotient Ψ×) of the domain. The log-shell construction only needs the perfection of the units and is unaffected by quotienting by torsion subgroups of units (see parts (ii),(iv),(v),(vi)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction of log(†F) as collection of ind-topological modules
rubrics_metrics.description: log(†F) := {log(†Fv)}_{v∈V} is the collection of ind-topological modules (constructed in preceding items) indexed by v ∈ V, equipped with group structure from additive portions of field structures and natural Gv(†Πv)-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: log(†F) packages the local log-objects into an F-prime-strip; related objects include I†F = {I†Fv}_{v∈V} the collection of log-shells. For v∈Vnon one may regard log(†Fv) as constructed only from the unit portion and its perfection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-links act only on local units / iterates defined on units
rubrics_metrics.description: Log-links (and iterates of log-links) are to be understood as being defined only on the (local) units that appear in domains of the log-links; when considering global fields embedded in idelic products, log-links are regarded as defined on products of groups of local units.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only reason for introducing log-links is to enable construction of log-shells from the various local units; construction of log-shells does not require 'non-unit' value-group portions of monoids. Thus in iterates one need only follow effect on groups of local units (Remark 1.1.1 (i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local units as Aut-holomorphic semi-germs (rigidity)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v ∈ Varc, the local units may be regarded as 'Aut-holomorphic semi-germs' (projective systems of neighbourhoods of units with induced Aut-holomorphic structures, group-structure germ, and a choice of one connected component), which are rigid and admit no nontrivial holomorphic automorphisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This viewpoint makes the Kummer/Kummer-type and idelic aspects robust and allows carrying over the approach to Kummer structures via Aut-holomorphic/co-holomorphicizations without change; also discreteness of logarithms of units ensures idelic aspects unaffected (Remark 1.1.1 (ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2 (i) — Coricity of associated D-prime-strips
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-link †F log−→ ‡F induces [poly-]isomorphisms †D ∼→ ‡D and †D(cid:3) ∼→ ‡D(cid:3) between associated D- and D(cid:3)-prime-strips; in particular it induces Ψcns(†D) ∼→ Ψcns(‡D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This asserts that while the log-link may be incompatible with multiplicative/additive ring structure across the link, it nevertheless induces compatible (poly-)isomorphisms at the level of the associated D-prime-strips (the ´etale-like/coric structures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2 (ii) — Compatibility with ring structures (local statements)
rubrics_metrics.description: At v∈Vnon, natural †Πv-actions on the Ψ’s are compatible with ind-topological ring structures on Ψ_{log(†Fv)}; at v∈Varc, the co-holomorphicizations determined by Ψ_{log(†Fv)}-Kummer structures on †Uv are compatible with the topological ring structures on Ψ and Ψ_{gp log(†Fv)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compatibility here is simultaneous: the diagrams relating Ψ†Fv and Ψ‡Fv respect the indicated ring/topological structures locally (cf. (∗non),(∗arc) diagrams).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2 (iii) — Compatibility with log-volumes
rubrics_metrics.description: At v∈Vnon the diagram is compatible with natural pv-adic log-volumes on subsets of †Πv-invariants of Ψ_{log(†Fv)}; at v∈Varc the diagram is compatible with angular log-volume on Ψ× and radial log-volume on Ψ_{gp log(†Fv)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'compatibility with log-volumes' is an invariance property allowing one to work with log-volumes consistently through composites of log-links/iterates (see Remarks 1.2.1 and 1.2.2 (v)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2 (iv) — Kummer theory incompatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer isomorphisms Ψcns(†F) ∼→ Ψcns(†D) and Ψcns(‡F) ∼→ Ψcns(‡D) fail to be compatible with the [poly-]isomorphism Ψcns(†D) ∼→ Ψcns(‡D) induced by the log-link, relative to the diagrams (∗non), (∗arc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concretely: Kummer-theoretic multiplicative structures are not transported compatibly across the log-link — an important obstruction used in subsequent arguments (cf. AbsTopIII Corollary 5.5 (iv)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.2 (v) — Holomorphic log-shells: local properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For v∈Vnon, I†Fv ⊆ log(†Fv) satisfies: (anon) I†Fv is compact (finite log-volume); (bnon) I†Fv contains the submonoid of †Πv-invariants of Ψ_{log(†Fv)}; (cnon) I†Fv contains the image of the submonoid of †Πv-invariants of Ψ× (pre-log-shell). For v∈Varc, analogous properties (aarc),(barc),(carc): compactness (finite radial log-volume), contains Ψ×, and image in Ψ_{gp log(†Fv)} is essentially the pre-log-shell.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are concrete compactness/containment properties of log-shells used in volume/logarithmic computations and to relate unit-submonoids to the constructed shells.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonarchimedean mono-analytic log-shells (Proposition 1.2 (vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: At v∈Vnon, algorithms construct an ind-topological module log(†D(cid:3)_v)=†Gv (cid:2) k∼(†Gv) and a topological submodule I†D(cid:3)_v = I(†Gv) ⊆ k∼(†Gv) (a 'mono-analytic log-shell') equipped with a pv-adic log-volume. There exist functorial Ism-orbits of isomorphisms log(†D(cid:3)_v) ∼→ log(†F (cid:3)×μ_v) and further isomorphisms ultimately relating log(†D(cid:3)_v) to log(†Fv) ∼→ Ψ_{gp ‡Fv}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are algorithmic/functorial constructions in the D(cid:3)-prime-strip yielding modules and submodules (log-shells) with compatible actions, log-volumes, and interrelations to F-side objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean mono-analytic log-shells (Proposition 1.2 (vii))
rubrics_metrics.description: At v∈Varc, analogous algorithms produce topological module log(†D(cid:3)_v)=k∼(†Gv) and topological subspace I†D(cid:3)_v = I(†Gv) ⊆ k∼(†Gv) with angular and radial log-volumes. There are functorial poly-isomorphisms log(†D(cid:3)_v) ∼→ log(†F (cid:3)×μ_v) and chains of poly-isomorphisms relating to log(†Fv) ∼→ Ψ_{gp ‡Fv}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Difference from nonarchimedean case: presence of angular and radial log-volumes and poly-isomorphism orbits (actions of {±1} on direct factors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mono-analytic log-shells (global collections) (Proposition 1.2 (viii))
rubrics_metrics.description: The local (vi),(vii) poly-/isomorphisms assemble into collections indexed by v∈V giving global maps log(†D(cid:3)) ∼→ log(†F(cid:3)×μ) ∼→ log(†F) ∼→ Ψ_{gp cns(‡F)} and corresponding identifications of collections of log-shells I†D(cid:3) ∼→ I†F(cid:3)×μ ∼→ I†F.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields coherent global identifications between D-side and F-side log-objects and their shells, equipped with natural Gv(‡Πv)-actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coric holomorphic log-shells (Proposition 1.2 (ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: If †F = ‡F = F(∗D) and the given log-link is the full log-link, there exists a functorial algorithm in the D-prime-strip ∗D constructing a collection of 'coric holomorphic log-shells' I∗D = I†F which may be identified with Ψ_{gp cns(∗D)} and come with natural isomorphisms (including I∗D(cid:3) ∼→ I∗D).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This asserts coric (´etale-like) constructions giving holomorphic log-shells functorially inside a D-prime-strip; these objects are central for later invariants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frobenius-picture / infinite chain of log-links (Proposition 1.2 (x))
rubrics_metrics.description: A chain of full log-links ... log−→ (n−1)F log−→ nF log−→ (n+1)F ... arises from a Z-indexed collection of distinct F-prime-strips, inducing chains of full poly-isomorphisms of associated D- and D(cid:3)-prime-strips. These chains can be represented by an oriented graph Γ admitting a natural Z-action (translation symmetry) that fixes the 'core' but forbids certain permutation symmetries (e.g., swapping adjacent vertices while fixing others).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This 'Frobenius-picture' organizes iterates of log-links into a combinatorial graph structure used in later invariant constructions; the lack of full symmetry is emphasized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concrete descriptions of log-shells in local fields (nonarchimedean/archimedean)
rubrics_metrics.description: For v∈Vnon with local field k: Ik := (p*_v)^{-1} · log_k(O×_k) ⊆ k, with inclusions Ok\{0} ⊆ Ok ⊆ Ik and log_k(O×_k) ⊆ Ik. For v∈Varc with k = C-like: Ik := {a∈k | |a| ≤ π} ⊆ k, with Ok\{0} ⊆ Ok ⊆ Ik and O×_k ⊆ exp_k(Ik).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These concrete models illustrate the abstract log-shell properties (compactness, containments, relations to exponential/logarithm) and show differing roles of log vs exp in nonarchimedean vs archimedean cases (Remark 1.2.2 (i),(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Upper semi-commutativity and log-volume commutativity on Γ
rubrics_metrics.description: Although the oriented graph Γ of iterated log-links fails to be commutative, the coric holomorphic log-shells exhibit 'upper semi-commutativity' — they contain/surject onto various images arising from composites of arrows in Γ; moreover, the diagram is 'commutative with respect to log-volumes,' allowing consistent use of log-volumes across composites (Remarks 1.2.2 (iii),(v)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This justifies working with invariants (e.g., log-volumes, arithmetic degrees) functorially across the Γ-diagram despite noncommutativity at the level of maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-wall: incompatibility with ring structures
rubrics_metrics.description: The log-link log(†Fv) → Ψ_{gp ‡Fv} is incompatible with the ring structures of Ψ_{gp †Fv} and Ψ_{gp ‡Fv}; it does not arise from a ring homomorphism. This 'log-wall' prevents transporting ring-dependent structures across the log-link by 'transport of structure'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consequences: conventional scheme-theoretic base-points and ´etale fundamental groups (Galois groups) are incompatible with the log-wall; Kummer theory (dependent on multiplicative structure) is also incompatible. The only manifestly compatible structure with the log-link is the associated D-prime-strip (Remark 1.2.4 (i),(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of structures incompatible with the log-wall
rubrics_metrics.description: Structures incompatible with the log-wall include (a) the additive structure on the image of the Kummer map (and similarly other ring/multiplicative-dependent structures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This underscores that multiplicative/additive ring-theoretic structures cannot be transported through log-links; one must instead pass through D-prime-strip/coric constructions.
